decision: Retain existing production kernels and dispatch rules. No tested candidate demonstrated a repeatable full-YOLO improvement large enough to justify replacing them.
findings: Larger K tiles reduced barriers but were mixed or slower across shapes; FP16 K=64 substantially regressed several common cases.
The 128-thread 8x4 layout did not improve full-model performance.

Existing 32x64 tiles improved several late/small or channel-tail microbenchmarks, but whole-model results varied: Node YOLO FP16 10.424->10.282 ms, Chrome 11.1->11.6 ms; the unchanged DepthART control also shifted in some comparisons.
Two subgroup prototypes were correct but slower on most tested shapes; this does not rule out better subgroup algorithms or benefits on other hardware/operators.
All recorded successful comparisons had finite outputs and maxDelta=0. Early prototype sweeps checked validation errors at the end; later runs checked them per pipeline and used NaN output sentinels.

Raw kernel timings use fixed recorded repeated dispatches and GPU timestamps. Model timings use recorded graphs, submit plus sync wall time; excludes camera and pre/post/presentation. Raw-kernel speedups are not model speedups.
Single-machine Apple M1 Pro / Metal observations do not establish cross-hardware performance.
